nodes.title: ► INFO
widgets_values:
# 2nd Pass ### Sampling *reference **INFO** box in 1st Pass* ### Upscaling - **upscale_factor** – defines upscale factor (1.0 = **no upscale**)
- **use_upscale_model** *(Ultimate Upscale always runs the selected model regardless)* **true** → uses selected upscale model **false** → regular upscale ### Tiled Sampling - **tile_size + tile_overlap** → only applies when **Tiled Diffusion** or **Ultimate Upscale** is used
- **tile_batch_size** – amount of tiles processed at once → reduce if low on VRAM
- **use_TD** *(Use Tiled Diffusion)* + **use_UU** *(Use Ultimate Upscale)* → regular sampling if both are set to **false**
**Tiled Diffusion** → faster → recommended denoise < 0.4
**Ultimate SD Upscale** → slower → recommended denoise < 0.3
### Color Correction > matches colors from previous pass - **strength**
→ 1.0 is usually good (0.0 = **off**)

nodes.title: ► INFO
widgets_values:
# Inpainting ### Sampling *reference **INFO** box in 1st Pass* ### Masking - **grow_mask**
– expands the provided masks
- **gaussian_blur**
– blurs the mask for smoother integration
- **crop_factor**
– multiple of the bbox area to be considered as context
→ usual range: 1.5 - 3.0
- **feather**
– softens the crop's edges for a smooth result
– also functions as noise_mask_feather
- **inpaint_size**
– temporary size of **Mask** area multiplied by **crop_factor** during generation
→ control over level of detail
→ disregarded when the masked area is larger already
- **noise_mask** ■ **enabled**    → context aware    → smooth, seamless result ■ **disabled**    → ignores context    → allows forcing out of context content    → requires further measures to blend in smoothly (_i.e. more inpainting_)    → denoise acts like opacity

nodes.title: ► INFO
widgets_values:
# ADetailer ### Sampling *reference **INFO** box in 1st Pass* ### ADetailer - **guide_size**
– size maximum for detections to be considered
→ allows skipping areas that are large/detailed enough already
→ disregarded when force_inpaint = **enabled**
- **max_size**
– temporary size the masked area is upscaled to during generation
→ control over level of detail
→ disregarded when the masked area is larger already
- **feather**
– softens the crop's edges for a smooth result
– also functions as noise_mask_feather
- **force_inpaint**
– bypasses threshold and size criteria when **enabled**
### Detection - **bbox_detector** *(UltralyticsDetectorProvider)*
(e.g. "face_yolov8m.pt")
– detects bbox containing the part to be ADetailed
- **sam_model**
(e.g. "sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth")
– segment-anything-model to crop the target part out of the bbox
- **segm_detector** *(UltralyticsDetectorProvider)*
(e.g. "person_yolov8m-seg.pt")
– detects the cropped out shape and masks correspondingly
- **bbox_threshold**
– probability of the detected part to match the query - faces : detected reliably → higher values work well ~ 0.7 - 0.8 - hands : more difficult to distinguish → lower values ~ 0.4 - 0.5
- **bbox_dilation**
– expansion of the detected bboxes
- **crop_factor**
– multiple of the bbox area to be considered as context
- **drop_size**
– size in pixels below which a detection will be disregarded
→ helps prevent after-detailing negligible background detections

nodes.title: ► INFO
widgets_values:
# Core Settings ### sage_attention - Enables/Disables SageAttention
→ requires [**Triton**](https://github.com/woct0rdho/triton-windows) and [**SageAttention**](https://github.com/thu-ml/SageAttention) to be installed
### easy_cache > Speeds up generation while lowering quality
→ lowering **reuse_threshold** reduces the speed increase, but preserves more of the original quality   ### compile_model - Processes the model to further speed up generation
→ initial compiling process takes some time *(few seconds in my experience)*, but the speed increase is noticeable
→ the compiling process is repeated under various obscure circumstances, e.g. when the latent size changes
### model_sampling_flux - **base_shift | max_shift**
higher values increase creative freedom during generation, but also the likelihood of deviations from the prompt
→ Flux Schnell models are only affected by **base_shift**
### DeDistilled Model - Enables use of regular CFG for DeDistilled models

nodes.title: ► Hello!
widgets_values:
—Hi, this is RedPinkRetro, welcome to **Flux Advanced !**— ► Built to provide an advanced, versatile and modular workflow for Flux with focus on efficiency, structure and information. ### Features : - Compatible with all common versions of Flux - Full metadata support; recognized by CivitAI - LoRA - SageAttention, EasyCache + Model Compile acceleration - ControlNet + Flux Tools *(alt. to CNet based on LoRA)* - Flux Redux *(similar to IPAdapter)* - PuLID (SVDQ-only) - Wildcard prompting - Installation and download guide for models and nodes - Multiple passes with upscale options and color correction > → 1st Pass : Detail Daemon + Variation Seed
→ 2nd Pass : DD. + Tiled Diffusion / Ultimate Upscale
→ ADetailer with dedicated LoRA Loader
→ Inpainting
More workflows like this can be found on my CivitAI page : — [RedPinkRetro/models](https://civitai.com/user/redpinkretro/models) **Thank you for your support!**

nodes.title: 2. SVDQuant Version
widgets_values:
## ► Nunchaku Installation (SVDQ) ### Automatic 1. Install the **ComfyUI-nunchaku** node pack and restart ComfyUI.
2. Open up and run the **Nunchaku_Installer** workflow, which contains a node that automatically installs the correct Nunchaku wheel for your system.
The *Installation Status* should something like

`✅ Successfully installed nunchaku-0.3.0+torch2.6-cp310-cp310-win_amd64.whl from GitHub Release.`

upon completion. > In case of download issues, try the other sources first.
If that doesn't help: - Check **ComfyUI-nunchaku**'s [**GitHub issues**](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/ComfyUI-nunchaku/issues) - Or **Manual Installation**   3. Done!
--- ### Manual 1. Download the correct [**Nunchaku wheel**](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/nunchaku/releases/tag/v0.3.0) corresponding to your Torch and Python version.
→ Both can be checked under ***System Info*** in the settings "*About*" section
2. Move the **.whl** file into `ComfyUI\python_embeded`
3. Open a command terminal in `ComfyUI\python_embeded` and install the wheel with this command modified to match your downloaded wheel's filename:

`python.exe -m pip install nunchaku-0.3.0+torch2.6-cp310-cp310-win_amd64.whl`

4. Done! --- ## Base SVDQuant models (*optional*) - [**Flux.1-Dev**](https://huggingface.co/mit-han-lab/svdq-int4-flux.1-dev/tree/main) | [**Flux.1-Schnell**](https://huggingface.co/mit-han-lab/svdq-int4-flux.1-schnell/tree/main)
→ to use a model all files of its directory should be downloaded and put into its own folder named: - "**svdq-int4-flux.1-dev**" - "**svdq-int4-flux.1-schnell**" respectively and placed in:
→ `ComfyUI\models\diffusion_models`
- [**T5xxl**](https://huggingface.co/mit-han-lab/nunchaku-t5/blob/main/awq-int4-flux.1-t5xxl.safetensors)
→ `ComfyUI\models\text_encoders`

### Input Image > paste the image to be inpainted here ### Mask > paste the same image here and mask the inpaint area via **MaskEditor**   ► **MaskEditor (BETA)**

The 2.5D comic illustration is portraying an exalted spellblade evoking a scene of holy allure.

She is thrusting upwards wielding a seraphic trident. The bladed pitchfork's straight shaft is wrapped in torn white fabric along its entire length.

Her thin frame is shrouded in a synthetic combat-jumpsuit with a pristine design, featuring a piece of flowing cloth attached to the side of her hip, as well as golden ornaments. Six wings with stained glass feathers unfurl behind her. The fabric's woven texture appears to shift in reaction to the surrounding lighting.

A foliate headset adorns her head, short light-made hair visible beneath.

Taking place within the derelict entry hall found in the heart of white tech-ruins of highly advanced origins. Flickering screens displaying glitched white imagery are hanging from wires coming from the ceiling.

The illustration's style is hand-drawn, using stylized proportions with dramatic shadows and high contrast. The color palette is combining intense hues.

A flat 2D minimalist digital painting of a crystal-cult fencer in a scene of clear allure.

She is swinging horizontally in a dynamic motion equipped with a selenite broadsword and slit-shield. Countless chains are attached to the asymmetrical shield's edge. Some chains appear glowing opalescent and give off a faint light.

Her thin frame is protected by a crystallized skeleton-armor with a savage appearance, featuring elegant chains attached to the pauldrons, as well as crystal rings. Long silver-trimmed slabs of diamond are attached to a wide metal belt around her small waist, covering her legs like layered armor-plating. Cuts and claw-marks on the armor's surface give it a rugged appearance.

She has wild crystallized hair styled into double-buns.

Taking place on top of the elevated aerie of a selenite tower enclosed by wrought iron balustrades, with a raven sitting on top of. Overlooking opalescent, foggy caverns, visible in the background.

The digital painting's style is hand-drawn, showcasing rough brushwork, using flat designs with lineless shapes as well as free form. The color palette is showing complementary hues inspired by fauvism.
